crosscoder: excellent reconstruction with graded decoder-norm asymmetry
no strict-exclusive Qwen feature under the published thresholds
aspd: shared and concentrated parameter-mechanism categories are measured
the strongest parameter-concentrated components remain semantically unresolved
global_summary.current_finding: The strongest current semantic overlaps do not coincide with the strongest ASPD parameter concentration.

phenomena.label: Hidden reasoning to visible answer boundary
phenomena.interpretation: Both methods retain contexts around the end of hidden reasoning and the onset of the visible answer.
limitations: ASPD component 736 is shared activation/shared mechanism, not a changed parameter mechanism.
No latent identity, vector match, or causal equivalence has been measured.

phenomena.label: Generic chat and turn boundaries
phenomena.interpretation: Retained contexts support a common qualitative family of chat, document, and response transitions.
limitations: The features and components are not aligned one-to-one.
The high-support ASPD examples in this group are mechanism-shared.

phenomena.label: Role-specific response onset
phenomena.interpretation: Crosscoder response-onset contexts have possible ASPD analogues in the same boundary-token family.
limitations: ASPD components 330 and 36 have only five validation fires each.
The relationship is a low-support hypothesis, not a measured match.

phenomena.label: ASPD-only parameter concentration
phenomena.interpretation: ASPD measures strong fine-tuned parameter concentration without a strict-exclusive Crosscoder counterpart.
limitations: Component 440 contexts are heterogeneous and have no stable semantic label.
Component 156 has a tentative numeric/document-initial interpretation, but its contexts remain heterogeneous.
No strict-exclusive corresponding Crosscoder feature was measured.
